source.title: Unified Pix Token And Word Token Generative Language Model

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; plotted figures are not rendered in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Applies image-only unsupervised pretraining in a new modality and reports a validation-loss result relevant to whether scaling behavior extends beyond text.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that training and validation loss converge with elapsed tokens, but does not fit or report a power law, vary model size or compute, or compare compute-optimal allocations. Only the validation-loss result is included as a row; the training-loss curve is not held-out loss.
record.test_reason: The study trains a single 120M-parameter model on one image-only dataset and shows its training and validation loss curves (Figure 8, no numbers). It does not vary parameters, data or compute, fit any power law, or extrapolate. Its statements that the model conforms to the scaling law are stated beliefs, not results. One loss-versus-tokens curve under a cosine schedule cannot show whether loss follows a power law in a scaling sense, so no version is tested. The reader's T3 and 'tests' are not justified.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that image-only pretraining of their 120M pix-token model converges, which they take to show feasibility and that the model learns pix-token patterns. They say they 'believe' it will follow generative-LM scaling laws with more parameters and data, but did not test this because compute was limited. The paraphrase should make clear that the scaling claim is untested speculation, not a finding.
record.recipe_differences: Image-only pixel-token unsupervised pretraining in one 120-million-parameter model; no multi-size scaling-law fit or compute-optimal allocation experiment.
record.problems: The paper states that compute resources were limited, the dataset was small and low resolution, and large-scale experiments could not be conducted. The reported loss curves have no numerical values in the supplied text, and there is no scaling sweep or control comparison.
record.rows_left_out: The training-loss curve in Figure 8 is not included because the claim concerns held-out loss; the paper describes it as converging with elapsed tokens but it is not a held-out measure.

untested.parts: All: no language-model scaling sweep or power-law fit.
All: no small-run fits or predictions of larger runs.
All: no architecture-shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
All: the study uses an image modality but reports one model size and one data size, with no power-law fit. Scaling is asserted as a belief only.

record.verdict_notes: Architecture proposal paper. The only experiment is one small run whose loss curves are shown in a figure without values. The comparison to GPT-3 convergence is qualitative. Scaling laws are mentioned only as an expectation, so the relation should be 'discusses' (T6) with no verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: Tests image rather than language-model pretraining and does not measure power-law loss scaling across parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits or predictions of larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation comparison or parameter/token scaling sweep.
No architecture comparison at fixed parameter count.

Only one small image-only unsupervised pretraining setup is reported. The paper does not establish a power-law form, test other modalities or training regimes, or scale across model sizes and compute.
No downstream task performance is measured.
No comparison of fitting choices, exponents, or curve departures.

rows.operation_detail: Measured validation loss over elapsed training tokens.

120000 image samples, about 6 billion pix tokens

rows.measure: Validation loss versus elapsed tokens; the paper says the curve converges like the training-loss curve.
rows.note: The text describes convergence but does not report numerical loss values or show that the curve follows a power law.
rows.check: A single run's validation curve, shown only in a figure, with one model size and no fit. It cannot show power-law scaling in parameters, tokens or compute for image models (V5) or any other version. The authors only say it 'converges like the training loss curve.' Keeping it as descriptive context is fine, but it should not link to V5.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The abstract, introduction, §4.2 and conclusion express an expectation of scaling with more parameters and data; the experiment does not test that expectation.

tranche.reason: One 120M-parameter model's convergence does not test any claim version. No power-law fit, scale comparison, extrapolation or compute-allocation experiment is reported.

source_check.notes: The text describes loss convergence but supplies no numerical loss values. The authors' scaling-law conclusion is an untested expectation; no verdict on V1–V7 is warranted.
